note: Hand-curated tax-and-revenue analysis of HB2, New Hampshire's omnibus budget policy trailer, for the 2021, 2023, and 2025 budget cycles. Candidates came from relevance-term matching over every extracted section (see working/.../hb2/{year}/); a human pass kept the tax/revenue sections, added three rate sections the matcher missed (flagged hand_added), and logged every exclusion. Roll-call votes are recorded on HB2 AS A WHOLE - a vote for or against the trailer is never a vote on one section, and must not be presented as one.

relevant_sections.heading: County Reimbursement of Funds; Limitations on Payments
relevant_sections.plain_language: Capped how fast county payments to the state for long-term care can grow (2 percent a year for the biennium) - the reimbursement stream counties raise through county property taxes.

relevant_sections.heading: Revenue Sharing; Suspension
relevant_sections.plain_language: Suspended revenue sharing with cities and towns (RSA 31-A) for another biennium - the general-fund aid stream that had been suspended in every budget since 2010.

relevant_sections.heading: Certain Differential Aid Calculations; Fiscal Year 2022
relevant_sections.plain_language: Let districts use their higher pre-pandemic or pandemic-year enrollment count for fiscal 2022 aid, so pandemic enrollment drops would not cut adequacy grants.

relevant_sections.heading: Transfer; Education Trust Fund
relevant_sections.plain_language: Moved $35 million of education trust fund surplus into a restricted account to fund additional school relief aid in fiscal years 2022 and 2023.

relevant_sections.heading: Education Trust Fund Created and Invested
relevant_sections.plain_language: Rewrote what the education trust fund may pay for - adequacy grants, the low and moderate income homeowners' property tax relief program, and the new education freedom accounts among them.

relevant_sections.heading: Transfer; Education Trust Fund
relevant_sections.plain_language: Transferred $1 million a year from the education trust fund to the public school infrastructure fund in each year of the biennium.

relevant_sections.heading: Distribution of Meals and Rooms Tax; Division of Travel and Tourism Development
relevant_sections.plain_language: Suspended the earmark that sends a slice of meals and rooms revenue to the state's travel and tourism division for the biennium.

relevant_sections.heading: State Aid Grants; Department of Environmental Services
relevant_sections.plain_language: Froze new state aid grants for local water, wastewater, and landfill infrastructure projects for the biennium (existing commitments kept) - deferring a municipal aid stream.

relevant_sections.heading: Revenue Stabilization Account; Cap
relevant_sections.plain_language: Raised the cap on the rainy day fund (revenue stabilization reserve) to 10 percent of general fund revenue, letting the state bank more surplus.

relevant_sections.heading: Rate
relevant_sections.plain_language: Began phasing out the interest and dividends tax: the 5 percent rate drops to 4 percent in 2023, 3 percent in 2024, 2 percent in 2025, and 1 percent in 2026 - the schedule the full repeal rides on.

relevant_sections.heading: Repeals; Interest and Dividends Taxation; 2027
relevant_sections.plain_language: Repealed the interest and dividends tax (RSA 77) outright, effective January 1, 2027 - the end point of the phase-out schedule. (The 2023 trailer later moved this date up to 2025.)

relevant_sections.heading: Imposition of Tax
relevant_sections.plain_language: Cut the meals and rooms tax rate from 9 percent to 8.5 percent, effective October 2021 - the tax's first rate cut; its revenue feeds the general fund, the education trust fund, and the towns' share.

relevant_sections.heading: Business Enterprise Tax; Returns
relevant_sections.plain_language: Raised the business enterprise tax filing thresholds to $250,000 of receipts or tax base, dropping the smallest businesses out of the filing pool.

relevant_sections.heading: Business Enterprise Tax; Rate Reduced
relevant_sections.plain_language: Cut the business enterprise tax rate from 0.675 percent to 0.55 percent for tax periods ending on or after December 31, 2022, and repealed the earlier revenue-trigger contingencies.

relevant_sections.heading: Business Profits Tax; Rate Reduced; Contingency Deleted
relevant_sections.plain_language: Cut the business profits tax rate from 7.7 percent to 7.6 percent for tax periods ending on or after December 31, 2022, deleting the contingency that could have raised it back to 7.9 percent.

relevant_sections.heading: Meals and Rooms Tax; Disposition of Revenue; Fund Established
relevant_sections.plain_language: Rewrote how meals and rooms tax money is shared: created the dedicated meals and rooms municipal revenue fund, with the towns' share (after administration and the education trust fund's cut) distributed to every city and town by population - the change that pushed the local share toward the statutory 30 percent.

relevant_sections.heading: Business Profits Tax; Credit Carry-forward Limited; Payments Due With Returns and Estimates
relevant_sections.plain_language: Limited how much overpaid business profits tax can be carried forward as a credit (to 500 percent of the current year's tax), with the rest refunded.

relevant_sections.heading: Business Enterprise Tax; Credit Carry-forward Limited; Payments Due With Returns
relevant_sections.plain_language: Applied the same 500 percent carry-forward limit and refund rule to business enterprise tax overpayments.

relevant_sections.heading: New Section; Commission to Study Limiting the Business Tax Credit Carry Over
relevant_sections.plain_language: Created a commission to study limiting the business tax credit carry-over - including whether unused credit refunds could be redirected to other uses.

relevant_sections.heading: Tax Expenditure Report; Weighted Apportionment Factors Removed
relevant_sections.plain_language: Updated the annual tax expenditure report statute - the report that tells lawmakers what each tax credit and exemption costs in forgone revenue.

relevant_sections.heading: School Building Aid; Annual Grant for Leased Space
relevant_sections.plain_language: Extended annual school building aid lease grants to more kinds of district lease arrangements.

relevant_sections.heading: New Paragraph; Kindergarten Adequate Education Grants
relevant_sections.plain_language: Made full-day kindergarten adequacy grants a standing charge on the education trust fund every year, ending the keno-revenue-dependent formula.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation; Department of Education
relevant_sections.plain_language: Appropriated $1.9 million to top up fiscal 2021 kindergarten and adequacy grant payments.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation; Department of Education
relevant_sections.plain_language: Appropriated $30 million from the education trust fund for school building aid on new projects - construction costs that otherwise land on local property taxes.

relevant_sections.heading: Education Tax Revenue; Fiscal Year 2023
relevant_sections.plain_language: Cut the statewide education property tax (SWEPT) for fiscal year 2023: the commissioner sets the rate to raise $263 million instead of the usual $363 million target - a one-year, $100 million property-tax reduction.

relevant_sections.heading: Supplemental Education Payment; Fiscal Year 2023
relevant_sections.plain_language: Guaranteed that no municipality's total education grant would fall because of the SWEPT cut: the state makes up any decrease with a supplemental payment.

relevant_sections.heading: American Rescue Plan Act; Unanticipated Revenue
relevant_sections.plain_language: Let municipalities accept and spend federal American Rescue Plan money as 'unanticipated revenue' without a town-meeting vote.

relevant_sections.heading: New Chapter; Education Freedom Accounts
relevant_sections.plain_language: Created the education freedom account (EFA) program - per-pupil adequacy money following students out of public schools, paid from the education trust fund; the fund's biggest new draw.

relevant_sections.heading: New Section; Business Enterprise Tax; Granite State Paid Family Leave Plan Tax Credit
relevant_sections.plain_language: Created a business enterprise tax credit worth 50 percent of premiums an employer pays into the new Granite State paid family leave plan.

relevant_sections.heading: Board of Tax and Land Appeals
relevant_sections.plain_language: Restated the Board of Tax and Land Appeals as a 3-member body of tax-law experts - the state board that hears property tax abatement appeals.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation; Public School Infrastructure Fund
relevant_sections.plain_language: Put $10 million from the education trust fund into the public school infrastructure fund for school construction and safety projects.

relevant_sections.heading: Taxation of Incomes; Rate
relevant_sections.plain_language: Rewrote the interest and dividends tax schedule to end at 3 percent in 2024: the previous 2 percent (2025) and 1 percent (2026) steps were deleted so the tax stops a full two years early.

relevant_sections.heading: Returns for Interest and Dividends Taxes; 2027
relevant_sections.plain_language: Moved the final interest-and-dividends return filing rules from 2027 to 2025 to match the accelerated repeal.

relevant_sections.heading: Amend Effective Date; Amend Repeal of Interest and Dividends Tax from 2027 to 2025
relevant_sections.plain_language: Changed the repeal's effective date: the interest and dividends tax now ends January 1, 2025 instead of 2027.

relevant_sections.heading: Revenue Sharing; Suspension
relevant_sections.plain_language: Suspended revenue sharing with cities and towns (RSA 31-A) for the 2024-2025 biennium - again.

relevant_sections.heading: Education Trust Fund Appropriations Reductions; Education Freedom Accounts
relevant_sections.plain_language: Reduced the education trust fund appropriation earmarked for education freedom accounts by $10 million in each year of the biennium, an accounting true-up to actual enrollment.

relevant_sections.heading: Education Trust Fund Created and Invested
relevant_sections.plain_language: Re-enacted the education trust fund statute, restating everything the fund may pay for - adequacy grants, homeowners' property tax relief, EFAs, court-ordered placements, and school building aid among them.

relevant_sections.heading: Special Education; State Aid
relevant_sections.plain_language: Changed special education state aid so districts are reimbursed for costs above 3.5 times the state average per-pupil cost - catastrophic costs that otherwise hit local budgets.

relevant_sections.heading: Liability for Children with Disabilities in Certain Court Ordered Placements
relevant_sections.plain_language: Shifted liability for certain court-ordered placements of children with disabilities, defining when the state rather than the school district pays.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation; Court Ordered Placements
relevant_sections.plain_language: Appropriated $9.2 million from the education trust fund for court-ordered placement costs.

relevant_sections.heading: Department of Education; Appropriation; CTE Renovation Projects; Sugar River Valley Regional Technical Center
relevant_sections.plain_language: Appropriated $12.5 million from the education trust fund for the Sugar River Valley career and technical education renovation project.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation
relevant_sections.plain_language: Appropriated $7.6 million from the education trust fund for the Winnisquam regional CTE renovation project.

relevant_sections.heading: Cost of an Opportunity for an Adequate Education
relevant_sections.plain_language: Rewrote the cost of an adequate education: base per-pupil aid rises to $4,100 with larger add-ons for free-and-reduced-lunch, special education, and English learners - the state share that offsets local school property taxes.

relevant_sections.heading: Extraordinary Need Grants; 2023
relevant_sections.plain_language: Rewrote extraordinary need grants for 2023 - extra aid scaled to a town's equalized property value per pupil, targeting the towns with the weakest tax bases.

relevant_sections.heading: Extraordinary Need Grants; 2025
relevant_sections.plain_language: Set the 2025-and-after version of extraordinary need grants, extending the property-poor-town aid formula.

relevant_sections.heading: Determination of Education Grants
relevant_sections.plain_language: Rewrote how each municipality's total education grant is determined, including hold-harmless rules so no town's grant falls below prior levels while the new formula phases in.

relevant_sections.heading: Business Profits Tax; Distribution to Education Trust Fund
relevant_sections.plain_language: Fixed the education trust fund's share of the business profits tax at 41 percent of revenue - replacing the old 'increase attributable to' formula with a straight statutory split.

relevant_sections.heading: Business Enterprise Tax; Distribution to Education Trust Fund
relevant_sections.plain_language: Fixed the education trust fund's share of the business enterprise tax at 41 percent of revenue, the same straight split.

relevant_sections.heading: Tax on Meals and Rooms; Population Figures
relevant_sections.plain_language: Updated the population-estimate process that determines each town's share of the meals and rooms tax distribution.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation; Department of Education; Kindergarten Adequate Education Grants
relevant_sections.plain_language: Appropriated $315,700 from the education trust fund for new full-day kindergarten adequacy grants.

relevant_sections.heading: Assessing Certification Board; Rulemaking and Implementation
relevant_sections.plain_language: Converted the assessing certification board into an advisory board inside the office of professional licensure - the body that certifies the assessors who set property values (companion sections 79:267-269 carry the details).

relevant_sections.heading: Revenue Information Management System Account
relevant_sections.plain_language: Extended the Department of Revenue Administration's revenue information management system account - the tax-collection IT system funded from the extra revenue it captures.

relevant_sections.heading: Department of Environmental Services; Appropriation
relevant_sections.plain_language: Appropriated $15 million in each of fiscal 2026 and 2027 for payments to communities for wastewater projects - state aid the 2025 trailer would later repeal before it was paid.

relevant_sections.heading: New Section; Study Commission Established
relevant_sections.plain_language: Created a study commission on the recent charitable gaming law changes, including the newly authorized historic horse racing machines - the fastest-growing state gaming revenue stream.

relevant_sections.heading: New Chapter; Video Lottery Terminals
relevant_sections.plain_language: Legalized video lottery terminals (slot-machine-style VLTs) at licensed charitable gaming facilities: the state collects 31 percent of gross machine revenue, split 75 percent to the general fund and 25 percent to the lottery's special fund - the budget's biggest new revenue source.

relevant_sections.heading: Education; School Money; Education Trust Fund Created and Invested
relevant_sections.plain_language: Amended the education trust fund's purpose list, including how court-ordered placement costs are paid.

relevant_sections.heading: Education; School Money; Education Trust Fund Created and Invested
relevant_sections.plain_language: Capped the education trust fund's balance: any surplus over $20 million at the close of a biennium is swept into the general fund.

relevant_sections.heading: Determination of Education Grants
relevant_sections.plain_language: Moved the final determination of education grants to October 1 and guaranteed each municipality at least 95 percent of its estimated grant.

relevant_sections.heading: Repeal
relevant_sections.plain_language: Repealed RSA 31-A, revenue sharing with cities and towns, outright - the municipal aid statute suspended in every budget since 2010 is now off the books entirely.

relevant_sections.heading: Repeal
relevant_sections.plain_language: Repealed the 2023 budget's $30 million in wastewater state aid payments to communities before the money went out.

relevant_sections.heading: Business Profits Tax; Distribution of Funds
relevant_sections.plain_language: Cut the education trust fund's share of the business profits tax from 41 percent to 39 percent, keeping more business tax revenue in the general fund.

relevant_sections.heading: Business Enterprise Tax; Distribution of Funds
relevant_sections.plain_language: Cut the education trust fund's share of the business enterprise tax from 41 percent to 39 percent.

relevant_sections.heading: Tobacco Tax; Distribution of Funds
relevant_sections.plain_language: Rewrote the tobacco tax split: 39 percent of tobacco revenue to the education trust fund, the rest to the general fund.

relevant_sections.heading: Tax on Transfer of Real Property; Distribution of Funds
relevant_sections.plain_language: Rewrote the real estate transfer tax split: 39 percent to the education trust fund, the rest to the general fund.

relevant_sections.heading: New Paragraph; Revenue Stabilization Reserve Account
relevant_sections.plain_language: Authorized drawing down the rainy day fund to cover a fiscal 2025 general-fund deficit, if the audit finds one.

relevant_sections.heading: New Paragraph; Taxation; Business Profits Tax; Credits
relevant_sections.plain_language: Created a 'granite patron of the arts' business profits tax credit for half of donations to the new state arts fund.

relevant_sections.heading: New Section; Business Enterprise Tax; Granite Patron of the Arts Credit
relevant_sections.plain_language: Let unused granite patron of the arts credits apply against the business enterprise tax.

relevant_sections.heading: Education; Adequate Education; Education Trust Fund; Annual Adjustment
relevant_sections.plain_language: Delayed the annual 2 percent inflation adjustment of per-pupil adequacy aid to July 2026 - a pause in the automatic growth of state school aid.

relevant_sections.heading: Education; Adequate Education; Education Trust Fund; Extraordinary Need Grants
relevant_sections.plain_language: Re-enacted the extraordinary need grant formula - the extra aid tied to a town's equalized property value per pupil.

relevant_sections.heading: New Section; Education; Adequate Education; Education Trust Fund; Fiscal Capacity Disparity Aid
relevant_sections.plain_language: Created fiscal capacity disparity aid: up to $1,250 extra per pupil for municipalities with less than $1 million of equalized property value per pupil, phasing out by $1.6 million - aid aimed squarely at property-poor towns.

relevant_sections.heading: Education; Adequate Education; Education Trust Fund; Determination of Education Grants
relevant_sections.plain_language: Rewrote how each municipality's education grant is computed to fold in the new fiscal capacity disparity aid.

relevant_sections.heading: Education; Special Education; State Aid
relevant_sections.plain_language: Restructured special education state aid administration and reimbursement - the catastrophic-cost aid that shields local budgets.

relevant_sections.heading: Education; Special Education; State Aid
relevant_sections.plain_language: Rewrote the funding rule for statewide special education programs.

relevant_sections.heading: Dedicated Funds; Amendments, Lapses, and Other Uses
relevant_sections.plain_language: Ordered the governor to raise general fund revenues or cut appropriations by a combined $16 million per year for the biennium, on top of the budget's line items.

relevant_sections.heading: Contingent Appropriation
relevant_sections.plain_language: Made an extra appropriation contingent on fiscal 2026 revenues beating the plan - surplus-triggered spending rather than committed dollars.

relevant_sections.heading: Board of Tax and Land Appeals; Quorum
relevant_sections.plain_language: Adjusted the Board of Tax and Land Appeals quorum rules - the board that hears property tax appeals, now also backstopping the housing appeals board.

relevant_sections.heading: Duties
relevant_sections.plain_language: Charged a study committee with weighing a state film office and an accompanying tax credit - a potential new tax expenditure.

relevant_sections.heading: Tax Amnesty
relevant_sections.plain_language: Created a tax amnesty program: back taxes paid during the amnesty window owe no penalties and only half the usual interest - a one-time revenue catch-up.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation
relevant_sections.plain_language: Appropriated $50,000 to the Department of Revenue Administration to run the tax amnesty program.

relevant_sections.heading: Department of Environmental Services; Appropriation
relevant_sections.plain_language: Appropriated $2.5 million in each of fiscal 2026 and 2027 for payments to communities - the much smaller replacement for the repealed $30 million wastewater aid.

relevant_sections.heading: Legislative Declaration of Authority Regarding Public Education
relevant_sections.plain_language: Declared the legislature's position on the Claremont school-funding rulings - asserting that defining and funding an adequate education is the legislature's prerogative, while the statewide education property tax and adequacy formula remain under active court challenge.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation; Department of Education
relevant_sections.plain_language: Appropriated $400,000 a year from the education trust fund for adult high school education programs.

relevant_sections.heading: Education; District Taxes; Reports Required; Cities and School Districts
relevant_sections.plain_language: Made the education and revenue departments jointly maintain school accounting standards - the books behind local school tax rates.

relevant_sections.heading: Appropriation; Department of Education
relevant_sections.plain_language: Appropriated $1.5 million a year from the education trust fund for statewide student learning platforms.

relevant_sections.heading: Operation of Keno Games
relevant_sections.plain_language: Removed the 11 a.m.-to-1 a.m. window on keno games, letting licensees run keno all business hours - keno revenue funds kindergarten aid.

relevant_sections.heading: New Section; Pari-Mutuel Pools, and Distribution of Tax Theron; Advanced Deposit Account Wagering
relevant_sections.plain_language: Authorized advance deposit account wagering on horse racing, with the tax on wagers flowing partly to the education trust fund.
